title: The Cognate Unlock & Vowel Soundboard
target_concept: Recognize shared Latin roots and steady five-vowel Spanish pronunciation in your very first sentences.

sentences.sentence_es: El hotel moderno es excelente.
sentences.translation_en: The modern hotel is excellent.
sentences.grammar_callout: Four of these five words are transparent cognates. Only 'el' (the) and 'es' (is) are structural glue.

sentences.sentence_es: La música clásica es fantástica.
sentences.translation_en: Classical music is fantastic.
sentences.grammar_callout: Spanish uses 'la' before general feminine nouns like 'la música' even when English omits 'the'.

title: Basic Subject-Verb-Object with Cognates
target_concept: Decode standard Subject-Verb-Object clauses where suffix bridges (-ción, -dad) unlock the nouns.

sentences.sentence_es: El profesor explica la situación.
sentences.translation_en: The professor explains the situation.
sentences.grammar_callout: The suffix -ción always maps to English -tion and is always feminine (la situación).

sentences.sentence_es: La universidad organiza una conferencia internacional.
sentences.translation_en: The university organizes an international conference.
sentences.grammar_callout: English -ty maps to -dad (universidad) and -nce maps to -ncia (conferencia).

title: Adjectives After Nouns
target_concept: Spanish names the thing first and describes it second: Noun + Adjective.

sentences.sentence_es: El director presenta un proyecto importante.
sentences.translation_en: The director presents an important project.
sentences.grammar_callout: Read 'un proyecto importante' as a single unit: first see the noun (project), then apply the modifier (important).

sentences.sentence_es: Las soluciones posibles requieren paciencia.
sentences.translation_en: The possible solutions require patience.
sentences.grammar_callout: Adjectives also echo plural endings: 'soluciones' (plural) pulls 'posibles' into the plural.

title: Negation & Question Markers
target_concept: Place 'no' directly before the verb to negate, and use inverted '¿' as an early heads-up for questions.

sentences.sentence_es: El sistema no funciona correctamente.
sentences.translation_en: The system does not work properly.
sentences.grammar_callout: Spanish has no helper verb like 'does'. Simply put 'no' immediately before the action verb.

sentences.sentence_es: ¿Necesita el equipo más información?
sentences.translation_en: Does the team need more information?
sentences.grammar_callout: The opening '¿' tells your internal reading voice to adopt question intonation before you even reach the first word.

title: Omitted Subjects (Verb Endings as Pronouns)
target_concept: Spanish drops subject pronouns ('I', 'we', 'they') because the verb ending already reveals who is acting.

sentences.sentence_es: Buscamos una oportunidad diferente.
sentences.translation_en: We are looking for a different opportunity.
sentences.grammar_callout: The ending '-mos' always means 'we' (nosotros). Also note that 'buscar' includes the 'for' inside the verb itself.

sentences.sentence_es: Prefieren estudiar en la biblioteca central.
sentences.translation_en: They prefer to study in the central library.
sentences.grammar_callout: A verb ending in '-n' (-an / -en) signals a plural 'they' (or plural 'you').

title: Clitic Object Pronouns
target_concept: Short object pronouns (lo, la, le, se, me) appear right before conjugated verbs or fuse onto the end of infinitives and gerunds.

sentences.sentence_es: El médico lo recomienda totalmente.
sentences.translation_en: The doctor totally recommends it.
sentences.grammar_callout: With conjugated verbs, 'lo' (it/him) jumps ahead of the verb: literally 'The doctor it recommends'.

sentences.sentence_es: Queremos explicárselo con calma.
sentences.translation_en: We want to explain it to him calmly.
sentences.grammar_callout: Pronoun Surgery: 'explicárselo' unpacks into 'explicar' (to explain) + 'se' (to him/her/them) + 'lo' (it).

title: El Problema en la Oficina
target_concept: Read a connected present-tense micro-story combining false cognates (soportar, carpeta) and clitic pronouns.

sentences.sentence_es: Actualmente Marco trabaja en una oficina muy activa.
sentences.translation_en: Currently Marco works in a very busy office.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'Actualmente' means 'currently', not 'actually'.

sentences.sentence_es: Guarda todos los contratos importantes en una carpeta azul.
sentences.translation_en: He keeps all the important contracts in a blue folder.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'carpeta' is a desk folder or binder, never a floor carpet.

sentences.sentence_es: Elena no soporta el ruido y decide explicárselo al director.
sentences.translation_en: Elena cannot stand the noise and decides to explain it to the director.
sentences.grammar_callout: Combines the false friend 'soporta' (tolerates) with the compound clitic verb 'explicárselo' (explicar + se + lo).

title: La Cena de mi Hermana
target_concept: Read a connected present-tense micro-story with the false cognates mayor, sopa, vaso and gripe, and the clitic 'me' before the verb.

sentences.sentence_es: Mi hermana mayor prepara una sopa caliente para la cena.
sentences.translation_en: My older sister prepares a hot soup for dinner.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'mayor' after a family word means older, not the mayor of a town. The adjective follows the noun: 'hermana mayor'.

sentences.sentence_es: Ella pone un vaso de agua fría al lado de cada plato.
sentences.translation_en: She puts a glass of cold water next to each plate.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'vaso' is a drinking glass, never a flower vase. 'Al lado de' (literally 'at the side of') means next to.

sentences.sentence_es: Yo tengo la gripe, así que no puedo comer mucho.
sentences.translation_en: I have the flu, so I cannot eat much.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'gripe' is the flu, not a grip. Spanish keeps the article: 'tengo la gripe'.

sentences.sentence_es: Mi hermana me trae té y me dice que descanse.
sentences.translation_en: My sister brings me tea and tells me to rest.
sentences.grammar_callout: The clitic 'me' jumps in front of the conjugated verb: 'me trae', 'me dice'. After a verb of telling someone what to do ('me dice que'), Spanish uses the subjunctive: 'descanse' is literally 'that I rest'.

title: Un Día en el Colegio
target_concept: Read a connected present-tense micro-story with the false cognates colegio, idioma, contestar and casualidad, and the clitics 'le' and 'lo'.

sentences.sentence_es: Todos los días Pablo asiste al colegio en autobús.
sentences.translation_en: Every day Pablo attends school by bus.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'asistir a' means to attend, not to assist, and 'colegio' is a school for children, not a college. 'Todos los días' (literally 'all the days') means every day.

sentences.sentence_es: Su idioma favorito es el inglés, pero también estudia francés.
sentences.translation_en: His favorite language is English, but he also studies French.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'idioma' is a whole language, not an idiom. Spanish does not capitalize language names: 'inglés', 'francés'.

sentences.sentence_es: La profesora le hace una pregunta difícil y él no sabe contestar.
sentences.translation_en: The teacher asks him a difficult question and he does not know how to answer.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'contestar' means to answer, never to contest. 'Hacer una pregunta' (literally 'make a question') is how Spanish says to ask a question, and 'le' marks who is asked.

sentences.sentence_es: Por casualidad, su amigo Luis conoce la respuesta y lo ayuda.
sentences.translation_en: By chance, his friend Luis knows the answer and helps him.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'casualidad' is chance or coincidence, not a casualty. The clitic 'lo' (him) stands before the verb: 'lo ayuda'.

title: El Misterio de la Librería
target_concept: Navigate past-tense narrative contrasts (ongoing imperfecto vs. completed pretérito) in a short story.

sentences.sentence_es: Llovía intensamente cuando Clara entró en la pequeña librería del barrio.
sentences.translation_en: It was raining heavily when Clara walked into the small neighborhood bookstore.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Llovía' (-ía imperfecto) paints the ongoing background weather, while 'entró' (-ó pretérito) marks the single completed action.

sentences.sentence_es: Buscaba una novela histórica pero encontró una carta antigua entre las páginas.
sentences.translation_en: She was looking for a historical novel, but she found an old letter between the pages.
sentences.grammar_callout: Again, '-aba' (buscaba = was looking for) sets the ongoing intention interrupted by '-ó' (encontró = found).

sentences.sentence_es: La lectura del documento reveló un secreto familiar extraordinario.
sentences.translation_en: Reading the document revealed an extraordinary family secret.
sentences.grammar_callout: Trap alert: 'lectura' means 'reading' (not lecture), and 'familiar' as an adjective means 'related to family' (not just well-known).

title: El Viaje Inesperado
target_concept: Follow a short past-tense story where the imperfecto sets the scene and the pretérito moves it forward.

sentences.sentence_es: Hacía mucho frío cuando Andrés llegó a la estación de tren.
sentences.translation_en: It was very cold when Andrés arrived at the train station.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Hacía' (imperfecto) describes the weather as a background state, while 'llegó' (pretérito) is the single completed arrival. Spanish says 'hace frío' (it makes cold) where English says 'it is cold'.

sentences.sentence_es: Quería comprar un billete, pero la máquina no funcionaba.
sentences.translation_en: He wanted to buy a ticket, but the machine was not working.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Quería' and 'funcionaba' are both imperfecto: ongoing states (a wish, a broken machine) rather than events. 'Billete' is a ticket in Spain; Latin America often says 'boleto'.

sentences.sentence_es: Entonces una mujer mayor le dio unas monedas y él pudo pagar.
sentences.translation_en: Then an older woman gave him some coins and he was able to pay.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Dio' and 'pudo' are pretérito: single events in the story. 'Pudo' means he managed to. Trap alert: 'mayor' is older here, not a town mayor.

sentences.sentence_es: Mientras esperaba el tren, decidió llamar a su familia.
sentences.translation_en: While he waited for the train, he decided to call his family.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Esperaba' (imperfecto) is the action in progress and 'decidió' (pretérito) is the new event that happens during it. Spanish 'esperar' already means 'wait for', so there is no word for 'for'.

title: La Fiesta de Cumpleaños
target_concept: Contrast habits in the past (imperfecto) with one-off events (pretérito) in a story with a surprise.

sentences.sentence_es: Cuando éramos niños, mi madre preparaba una fiesta enorme cada año.
sentences.translation_en: When we were children, my mother used to prepare a huge party every year.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Éramos' and 'preparaba' are imperfecto: a habit or repeated situation in the past, which English often renders with 'used to'. 'Cada' (each, every) never changes: 'cada año'.

sentences.sentence_es: Ese año, sin embargo, la tarta se cayó al suelo.
sentences.translation_en: That year, however, the cake fell on the floor.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Se cayó' (pretérito of 'caerse') is a single accident: the habit is over. 'Sin embargo' is a fixed phrase meaning however, even though its words literally say 'without obstacle'.

sentences.sentence_es: Todos nos reímos, aunque mi madre estaba muy triste.
sentences.translation_en: We all laughed, although my mother was very sad.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Nos reímos' is pretérito (a moment of laughter), while 'estaba' is imperfecto: her sadness is the ongoing state behind it. 'Reírse' (to laugh) always takes the reflexive 'nos/se'.

sentences.sentence_es: Esa noche mi padre compró otra y la fiesta continuó hasta la madrugada.
sentences.translation_en: That night my father bought another one and the party went on until dawn.
sentences.grammar_callout: 'Otra' stands for 'otra tarta': Spanish drops a noun that was just mentioned. 'Compró' and 'continuó' are both pretérito, a chain of completed events that closes the story.
